sections.overview: Neolebias lozii is a very small freshwater fish known only from Zambia’s Upper Zambezi drainage.
sections.identification: The recorded maximum is 1.8 centimetres standard length.
sections.habitat: It occurs in small streams associated with seasonally flooded plains and dense submerged or emergent vegetation.
sections.diet: FishBase reports that it feeds on tiny aquatic invertebrates.
sections.behavior: Its small size and association with dense stream-margin plants are documented, but other species-specific behavior remains poorly known.
sections.reproduction: The sources consulted do not provide a reliable species-specific account of its breeding cycle.
sections.ecology: The fish is restricted to a few tributaries on the eastern side of Zambia’s Barotse Floodplain, where maintaining stream flow and riparian vegetation is important.
sections.conservation: FishBase reports a Critically Endangered IUCN assessment from 2007; the assessment highlights its extremely restricted range and habitat vulnerability.
